articles.title: How to email a customer when their Stripe payment fails
articles.excerpt: When a renewal fails, Stripe fires invoice.payment_failed and starts retrying. Its recommended setting tries up to 8 times in two weeks. Unless you've turned on Stripe's own email, your customer has n…
articles.body: When a renewal fails, Stripe fires invoice.payment_failed and starts retrying. Its recommended setting tries up to 8 times in two weeks. Unless you've turned on Stripe's own email, your customer has no idea. It's usually an expired card, not someone leaving, and I think those quiet two weeks are where you lose people who meant to stay. Below is the email I'd send the same day, and the few lines that send it. The short answer When a payment for an invoice fails, Stripe sends an event called invoice.payment_failed . Stripe's own advice is to notify the customer. You can turn on Stripe's email, handle the event in your own code, or connect Stripe to Kicklace and let it write and send a note in your voice. Whatever you pick, tell the customer quickly and plainly.

articles.title: OpenClaw: Moving from AI Libraries to Agent Runtimes
articles.excerpt: For most developers, building an AI agent starts with a library. You import a framework like LangChain or CrewAI, define a chain of prompts, and execute a script. However, this "request-response" mode…
articles.body: For most developers, building an AI agent starts with a library. You import a framework like LangChain or CrewAI, define a chain of prompts, and execute a script. However, this "request-response" model creates a fundamental limitation: the agent only exists for the duration of the script's execution. Enter OpenClaw , an MIT-licensed, open-source framework that shifts the paradigm from an AI library to an AI runtime . Instead of being a set of tools you call within your code, OpenClaw acts as a persistent background daemon—essentially an "Agent OS"—that manages the lifecycle, memory, and communication of autonomous agents. The Architectural Shift: Runtime vs. Library The core distinction between OpenClaw and industry-standard orchestration tools is the execution model.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.

articles.title: Halley's Comet dazzles from afar in spectacular astrophoto of Orionid meteor shower
articles.excerpt: This incredible composite image of Orionid meteors was captured as Earth passed through the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet.
articles.body: Tim McCollum captured a stunning view of Orionid meteors in the early hours of Oct. 21. (Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. McCollum was able to capture a trio of vivid Orionid meteors as they streaked through the night sky above the city of Toccoa, Georgia, between 3-4 a.m. on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.
